key_insight: A parity-breaking cellular automaton built from chiral collisions and velocity rotations coarse-grains to hydrodynamics with odd viscosity, linking microscopic chirality to macroscopic odd-fluid behavior.
engineering_relevance: This offers a particle-based route to model and study transport in parity-violating fluids, potentially useful for designing active, magnetic, or chiral transport systems.
method: Modified the 2D FHP lattice gas automaton with chiral two-body collision rules.
Systematically rotated particle velocities to emulate a background magnetic field and break parity.
Derived the resulting coarse-grained hydrodynamic transport coefficients, including odd viscosity.
evidence_signal: The analytical transport coefficients were verified against Poiseuille-flow simulations of the chiral FHP automaton.
watch_item: As a lattice-based idealization, the model’s quantitative relevance may depend on how well the chosen collision and rotation rules capture a real physical parity-breaking mechanism.
paper_title: Odd fluids from chiral cellular automata
